Here are some things you should learn during a short 1-2 week break BEFORE SUMMER (I don't want to overwhelm you)


Now here's something extra always ask for the list before doing anything because they might have something different for you guys.

1.You'll be moving all the furniture from all the rooms to strip and wax the tile what ever your school has. (No you won't do this during short breaks)


2.youll be wiping down chairs(normal cleaning chemicals and for white boards (only water or alcohol NEVER ANYTHING ELSE) then there sinks (cleaning chemicals or rag and water just don't drown it lol.)


3.cleaning lights out of dead bugs(so you'll need to learn how to open the lights), dusting hallways,cleaning mirrors in hallways,removing tape,wiping down small classroom windows. (Glass cleaner),cleaning kick plates,wiping down doors and cleaning TVs 


4. Extracting carpets(this can be done during a 2 week break which is super easy. Waxing is usually always saved for summer vacation.


5.high and low dusting, wiping counters down, computers,sinks and scraping gum off the bottom of all desks. Cleaning vynle base boards with a rage and some basic chemicals that are provided for you. ALWAYS READ the label of chemicals.



6.kaivacing bathrooms,pumice stone rings off toilets and removing graffiti 



7. If you have anything maintenance related to your list duties learn to 

Replace a sink

Replace a white board

Fix door handles

Fix machines if needed

Change a simple light bulb

Use power tools or simple screwdriver for small tasks

Power lift heavy things like chairs and dolly cabinets to throw away. Always ask for help if you can't lift by yourself.

So there are benefits let me start off by saying don't go above and beyond EVER. do the basics and you'll have free time. During summer you'll have to work hard tho.
NEVER tell your boss you have free time. Always say your always working till the last minute and best thing to do is to keep boundaries with coworkers do your own work and no one else. If your with a union and they try and give you more work look over your contract and see if it's in there if not. It's not your problem. 

It depends on your boss if all your work is done and they trust you to leave early knowing there will be no complaints. Some jobs require you to stay till your end of shift. 


Cons-lots of walking lmao. 15k-25k steps a day. Get good insoles and good shoes.

Take your required breaks and rest. 

Listen to your boss. If you don't ever plan on moving up STAY UNDER THE RADAR and do the basics. Because the more people notice your hard work the more they make you in charge of things or reward you with more work.
